disposition: R4b is preserved as an operational incident. R4c starts from a new preregistration, study instance, schedule identities, SQLite database, and output root; no R4b cell or response is reused.

r4c_protocol_change.rationale: Every normalized R4b transport request was at most 8,017 UTF-8 bytes, yet both providers reported more than 2,048 input tokens for 34 completed calls. R4c reserves 8,192 input tokens per transport, a conservative ceiling above the entire normalized request byte length even under a one-byte-per-token upper-bound thought experiment. UTF-8 bytes remain a transport diagnostic and are not relabelled as measured tokens; actual usage continues to come from the provider response.
r4c_protocol_change.post_receipt_resource_policy: A response received above a local cap is retained, traced, parsed, and scored. It is reported separately as a post-receipt resource-policy violation and cannot pass end-to-end conformance.

resource_ledger.policy: R4c cap enforcement carries forward the complete conservative prior entering R4b, every observed R4b call and transport, every provider-reported R4b token, every relevant R4b output envelope, and the conservative R4b cost projection.

claim_boundary: R4c measures synthetic evidence binding, one-rule decision fidelity, response-contract reliability, and trace acknowledgement under the amended resource envelope. It does not measure hydraulic validity, ecological benefit, field performance, practitioner usefulness, prompt-injection resistance, broad production safety, or production release readiness.
